could_not_do: RI-UIX09 P4's fill bar (D2 >= 0.35) IS NOT MET AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT IS. On my instrument the live inventory panel reads ~0.15 with 22 pictorial elements in it, where round 1 read 0 pictorial. My D2 is NOT comparable to the round-1 critic's numbers — it reads the journal at 0.13 where the critic read 0.349 on a journal neither of us changed, so the two instruments differ by more than the effect. THE ONLY VALID COMPARISON IS MINE-TO-MINE across the delete-the-fix arms, which is why the control arm exists. Treat any live-vs-round-1 fill delta in this piece as unmeasured.

THE PANEL IS TOO BIG FOR ANY CONTENT A LIST CAN PUT IN IT, and this is a finding for the round-2 critic rather than an excuse. RI-UIX03 P5 caps the panel at 60% of the frame and this build sits at 57.2%; Morrowind's inventory window in REF-A12b-inventory__mw-15538700.jpg is about 24% of its frame and is sized to its contents. RI-UIX09 P4's 0.35 was read off windows sized that way. Filling 57.2% of a 1920x1080 frame to 0.35 from a 44-item sortable list needs roughly 415,000 px^2 of drawn matter and the honest content available comes to about half that. I did NOT close the gap with decorative fill; the brief forbids it and it would have been the wrong screen. RI-UIX09's own provenance note says 0.35 is the number to challenge, and this is the challenge, with the arithmetic.

RI-UIX07 harness field `elements[].withdrawn_because` is DELIBERATELY NOT implemented as written. A withdrawn element is not in `elements`, and a placeholder there would break E-T5 outright — the census-identity test requires the combat element list to be identical id-for-id to one taken with the world set deleted. The withdrawal is reported at `getUIState().hud.world.withdrawn` instead.

RI-UIX07 W4's spell mark is a CHARGE (focus held / attuned spell cost), not Morrowind's cast chance. This build has no to-hit roll on a cast (RI-MAG01 §E forbids one), so there is no cast probability to draw. Named `charge` in the census so nobody reads a probability off it.
RI-UIX07 §G (V11) and RI-UIX09 DN7 (the blind pair) are judge gates. Rule 0 forbids spawning a session and rule 25 forbids judging a pack I built. Not run; the round-2 critic owns them.

E-T3's permitted <=250 ms RETURN fade is not built. Stricter than the item requires, stated so its absence is not read as an oversight: building it would add a second clock beside E-T4's one clock and buy nothing the census can see.

I proceeded past `node tools/contention.mjs` exit 3 (`WAIT — the box is at or over its ceiling`) for the control arm, because the ceiling was reached partly by my own deadlocked waiter processes, which I then killed by PID. Recorded as rule 21 requires.

THE DELETE-THE-FIX CONTROL ARM REACHED 7 OF 8 SCREENS. The container-name guard did NOT run on it, so the claim 'the `undefined` header comes back when the fix is removed' is UNMADE — the root cause is read off the source (`String(undefined)` in `Engine.openContainer`) and the live arm shows all four bad values refused, and that is one arm of the two.

MY OWN D1-OBSERVED MEASUREMENT IS INERT AND THE CONTROL ARM IS WHAT PROVED IT. RI-UIX09 method 3 wants '>= 3 distinct hues that is NOT GLYPH INK' and I did not implement the clause after the comma; the control's inventory — a measured zero pictorial elements — scores 15 of 15 rows passing, worst row 3 hues, because a row's leading 48 px already holds the woven ground, the name's ink, the shell inlay and the anti-aliasing between them. Both arms are the positive arm. So the observed half of D1 is reported as `inert`, not as a pass, and the declared half (method 2, off the element census) is the only D1 figure this piece stands behind. The fix is written above `distinctHues` in the tool so it is not re-derived.

MY D2 IS NOT THE ROUND-1 CRITIC'S D2 AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE SUBTRACTED. On the journal — a screen neither of us changed — the critic read 0.349 and I read 0.1315. The instruments differ by more than any effect I could have produced, so the round-1 fill figures quoted in the dispatch are not a baseline for mine. The journal is also the piece's repeatability check and it passes: control 0.1311, live 0.1315, a difference of 0.0004 on a screen I did not touch.

The narrow-viewport (844x390) pass had not completed when this was written. The dial's geometry at that viewport is derived rather than photographed: `dialGeometry` clamps the radius to 42.9 px there and `cy = H - 42*s - r`, so `y + h = 374.8` against `H/2 = 195` — D1 holds by arithmetic, not by picture, and that is a weaker claim.

`hud.place` renders the raw cell id (`thorn-hall`), not a display name — visible in the world capture. RI-UIX07 W5 asks for 'the name of the cell you just entered' and this IS that value; whether Black Marsh's cells should carry a separate display name is a data question I did not invent an answer to.

THE CONTAINER SCREEN'S NEW SELECTED-ITEM BAND HAS NEVER BEEN RENDERED, and rule 10 is explicit that confirming the code runs is my job, not the critic's. The container capture in `screens/live-container__1920x1080.png` was taken at 09:06, BEFORE the band landed in b876c46c97, so it shows the twelve-row-plus-band layout's predecessor. `node tools/boot-check.mjs` passes but only renders the world, so `drawContainer` has not executed since the edit. A focused render was launched and had not returned when this was written — the box was at load ~20 over 4 cores for the last hour. **Treat the container band as unexecuted code.** Cheapest check for whoever picks it up: `node tools/ui/t4-r2-measure.mjs --label live` reaches the container twice (named and unnamed) and will throw there if it is broken. Everything else in the container change — the icons on both sides and `containerTitle()` — IS exercised by the 09:06 capture and by the live guard sweep.

The control arm was still running when this was written and had reached 4 of 8 screens; EVIDENCE.md carries whatever it had produced at generation time and names the rest under 'what is missing'. `tools/ui/t4-r2-evidence.mjs` regenerates the document from the JSONs, so re-running it after the arm finishes costs one command and no judgement.
